clue.text: School does something to get mutual agreements

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive school, the standard UK state secondary
acts means does something, takes action

explanation.surface: A school taking action in order to reach agreements with others.
explanation.definitionFit: Compacts are formal agreements or pacts made between parties, each bound to the other.

clue.text: Nothing well-balanced in old-style qualification

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
level means even, well-balanced

explanation.surface: Having no balanced approach in an outdated exam.
explanation.walkthrough: O levels were British school exams taken at about sixteen, replaced by GCSEs in 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: The O level was a British school exam taken at about sixteen before GCSEs replaced it.

clue.text: Picture of little dog that's kept at home

indicators.note: kept means held within, so the small dog holds the words for being at home

parts.note: a pup is a young, small dog
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A photo of a puppy that is kept indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a picture pinned to a wall, typically of an idol or glamorous figure.

clue.text: Fellow traveller maybe three miles south of mountain pass

indicators.note: in a down answer, south of means placed below, so the three miles sit under the pass

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountain peaks
a league is an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: A travelling companion walks three miles south of a mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-worker is a fellow in the same job; a fellow traveller is one example of a companion.

clue.text: Snake now more than half twisted

indicators.note: only the leading stretch, more than half the word for now, is twisted round to run backwards

parts.note: the present is now, the current time

explanation.surface: A snake that is at present mostly coiled.
explanation.walkthrough: The first four of seven letters, PRES, are turned to SERP; ENT stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent is a snake, especially a large one, in literary language.

clue.text: Fantasies? Daughter has lots

parts.note: reams means lots, a great quantity, as in reams of paper

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a daughter has a lot of fantasies.
explanation.definitionFit: Daydreams and fantasies are the same flights of imagination, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Resolute, not half, or put off?

indicators.note: not half says the second half of the word for resolute is dropped

parts.note: determined means resolute, firm of purpose

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a person is resolute, half-hearted, or simply discouraged.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone from acting is to deter them.

clue.text: Old church getting fifty in season? Wonderful!

parts.note: ex means former, old, as in an ex-wife
CE is the Church of England
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
Lent is the church season before Easter

explanation.surface: An old church raising fifty pounds in Lent: marvellous!
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are exclamations of delight at something superb.

clue.text: Fellow with UK country relations is a model

parts.note: a man is a fellow, a chap
NI is Northern Ireland, one of the four countries of the United Kingdom
kin are relations, family

explanation.surface: A man with relatives in a UK nation works as a model.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannikin is a figure or dummy used to display clothes, i.e. a model.

clue.text: Army officer's spoken with heart

indicators.note: spoken says the army officer's title is heard rather than written, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer, a title pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: An army officer talks with feeling, from the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The kernel of something is its essential core or centre, just as its heart is.

clue.text: Modest collection of two notes and a coin?

parts.note: re and ti are two notes of the sol-fa scale
a cent is a small coin, a hundredth of a dollar

explanation.surface: A small hoard of two banknotes and a single coin would be a modest collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like banknotes beside 'coin', but they are musical notes of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticent person is reserved and holds back from showing off, which is being modest.

clue.text: Planned action creating a bit of a scene

definitions.meaning: in football, a rehearsed move from a free kick or corner
an elaborately staged episode in a film, play or novel

explanation.surface: A rehearsed move that causes a small commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Set piece covers both a rehearsed sporting move and a showpiece section of a drama.

clue.text: Report of broadcast relocated

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for broadcast is taken by its sound

parts.note: relayed means broadcast, passed on by transmission

explanation.surface: A report about a broadcast that was moved to a different slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid again in a new place, like a carpet or track, has been moved and put down elsewhere.

clue.text: Village to be excited about store finally offering something for the kitchen

indicators.note: letters excited and stirred about are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word store

explanation.surface: Villagers are thrilled that their shop is at last selling something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited about' shuffles VILLAGE, TOBE and E, the last letter of 'store'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking oil pressed from plants is a staple kept in the kitchen for frying.

clue.text: Guessing discharge has uranium? Get on the phone!

parts.note: to vent is to discharge or let out
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: Speculating that a leak contains uranium, someone urges a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Venturing a guess means offering a speculative answer, so the participle fits guessing.

clue.text: Bishop guided around that place chatted

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: around says the word for guided surrounds the word for that place

parts.note: led means guided
there means that place, as opposed to here

explanation.surface: A bishop showing people round a place chatted away.
explanation.walkthrough: Blether is a Scots word for idle talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To blether is to talk at length and idly, Scots for prattling or chatting.

clue.text: Jazz fan hanging round about — I have to be artistic

indicators.note: hanging round means surrounding, so the jazz fan's word goes round the word for about

parts.note: a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
re means about, concerning
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A jazz lover hanging about declares he has to be arty.
explanation.definitionFit: Creative and artistic both describe someone with imagination who makes original work.

clue.text: Member of royal family can rebel with trip abroad

indicators.note: abroad means widely scattered, so these letters are spread out and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A royal might rebel by taking a trip overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria's consort was a member of the British royal family by marriage.

clue.text: Learning the alphabet?

definitions.meaning: the alphabet is made up of the characters A to Z

explanation.surface: A child learning the ABC.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters means both scholarship and the characters from A to Z.

clue.text: One of three in a boat somewhere off the Scottish mainland

definitions.text: One of three in a boat
definitions.meaning: one of the trio in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat, with George and J
the southern part of the island of Lewis and ... in the Outer Hebrides

explanation.surface: One of three people in a boat off the coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a character in Jerome's novel and to a Hebridean island.

clue.text: High flier in trouble heading off to meet old singer

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter, the head, of the high flier's name is removed

parts.note: Icarus, in Greek myth, flew too near the sun and fell when his wax wings melted

explanation.surface: A high flier in difficulty sets off to meet a veteran singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Caruso was a celebrated Italian operatic tenor of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Happily puffed up?

parts.note: walking on this means being blissfully happy, and something puffed up is filled with gas; it also means being broadcast

explanation.definitionFit: Walking on it is being elated, and a puffed-up balloon holds the gas we breathe.

clue.text: A tin hat I designed for islander

indicators.note: designed means newly fashioned, so these letters are reshaped into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A helmet created for someone who lives on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Tahiti in French Polynesia is an inhabitant of that Pacific island.

clue.text: Cautious little girl turning up to support little boy

indicators.note: in a down answer, to support means to sit underneath, so the girl's name goes below the boy's

parts.note: Tim is a short boy's name, as in Tiny Tim

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

explanation.surface: A shy little girl appears to back up a small boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid person is fearful and hesitant, so is cautious about acting.

clue.text: It sounds like Mrs Fawlty had to make a hissing sound

indicators.note: these words say the phrase that follows is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Sybil Fawlty is the hotelier's wife in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers; had means ate, so she had a meal

explanation.surface: Sybil Fawlty supposedly had to hiss, in the manner of the hotel's formidable landlady.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a 1970s British sitcom; Sybil is Basil Fawlty's sharp-tongued wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To sibilate is to utter an s or sh sound, a hiss through the teeth.

clue.text: Observe one of estranged couple in film rolling over

indicators.note: rolling over means turning back to front, so the name is read backwards

parts.words: one of estranged couple in film
parts.note: Kramer vs Kramer is a 1979 film about a divorcing couple, each surnamed Kramer

explanation.surface: Someone notes that one half of a separated screen couple is turning over.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark something is to notice it, or to comment on what has been noticed.

clue.text: One promising not to start book

indicators.note: not to start says the first letter is dropped from the word for one who promises

parts.note: a pledger is someone who makes a pledge, a promise

explanation.surface: Someone who promised not to begin a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An accounts book in which transactions are entered is the classic bookkeeping record.

clue.text: I'd hissed — terrible bit of food on the table!

definitions.text: bit of food on the table

indicators.note: terrible means in a dreadful state, so these letters are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner hisses at an awful accompaniment served up at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A small extra dish served alongside the main course is a portion of food on the table.
